newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices ease on higher imports.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices ease on higher imports.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices eased during the week on increased arrivals of imported oil from the U.S., Malaysia and Argentina, traders said on Wednesday.
"Prices have eased to some extent as a lot of vessels with imported oils are arriving," O.P. Goenka, a senior official in the Central Organisation for Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT).
"A vessel with imported oil is arriving every alternate day," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 36,000 rupees per tonne, compared with 36,200 rupees last week. Palm olein oil was quoted at 28,200 rupees, after 28,900 last week.

Industry officials said imports of large quantities were taking place, despite good crop arrivals, due to a rise in domestic demand. "Indian domestic supply is not catching up with the demand," Shah said.
Goenka said prices would start firming from June once domestic supplies started slowing.
COOIT officials expect edible oil imports in the 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) season to rise to about 1.4 million tonnes from 1.14 million in 1995/96.
